hedges.reason: o1 is the closest match to Tread in the list: a crypto trading-terminal and execution venue with a points program and an expected governance-token launch. Both teams face the same launch conditions: the same listing venues (Binance Alpha, mid-tier exchanges, Hyperliquid spot), the same market makers, and the same crowd of airdrop farmers. When the market is risk-on and new airdrop tokens hold their price, both are pushed to bring their launches forward. The worlds where Tread launches early are the worlds where o1 is most likely to launch by the middle rung.

GRVT is a points-farming perp DEX, in the same exchange and trading-venue category as Tread. Its launch timing depends on the same things: perp volumes, listing appetite for new venue tokens, and whether recent perp-DEX launches traded well. A hot market that pushes Tread to a Q3 launch also makes it easier for GRVT to launch in 2026.

Solstice is another points-program DeFi protocol waiting for a launch window. It is a weaker match on product (yield and stablecoin rather than trading), but its timing depends on the same airdrop-demand and liquidity conditions. It widens the basket so the hedge does not rest on a single team's idiosyncratic delays.

claims.reason: A Tread launch by September 30 would most likely come from a window where venues are listing trading-terminal and exchange tokens and airdrop tokens are holding their price. o1 is a close peer with the same investors and farmer base and faces the same incentive to launch while that window is open. So a Tread launch in Q3 and an o1 that stays unlaunched through the middle rung should rarely happen together.

The same mechanism applies to GRVT. A perp-DEX and trading-venue launch cycle strong enough to pull a smaller platform like Tread to market by Q3 should also pull forward GRVT, a larger and more advanced points-program perp DEX. The chance of GRVT staying unlaunched in that world is lower, though team-specific delays remain possible.
